small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 configs (and BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=128) — at M=N=K=8192 the GEMM is compute-bound and bigger K-tiles reduce pointer arithmetic and overlap loads better.
- The softmax row width N=8192 with BLOCK=8192 forces num_warps=16 and a full row in registers, which is heavy register pressure; try BLOCK=8192 with num_warps=8 and num_stages=3, or switch to a two-pass online softmax (max+sum streaming, then normalize) with BLOCK=2048 and num_warps=8 to reduce spills.
- Mask the GEMM loads on the K boundary only when K%BLOCK_K!=0; here K=8192 is divisible by all BLOCK_K candidates, so the unmasked loads are fine — but ensure offs_m/offs_n masking on A/B loads when adding configs whose tiles don't divide M/N.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax into the GEMM epilogue using a split-N persistent design: have one program own an entire row tile (BLOCK_M rows × full N), iterate N tiles in the inner loop computing matmul+bias+GELU, keep running row-max and row-sumexp in registers (online softmax), then a second pass over N tiles re-streams the GELU output and writes normalized values. This eliminates the full 1024×8192 fp32 intermediate write/read between GEMM and softmax (~256MB of traffic).
- Alternatively, do a two-kernel design where the GEMM writes the GELU output and also writes per-row max+sumexp computed on-the-fly via atomics or via a per-row-tile reduction buffer, so the softmax kernel only does a single normalize pass instead of max+sum+normalize.
- Consider using tf32 (`tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=True)`) or fp16 accumulation paths if precision tolerance allows — at 8192³ this dominates runtime.
